method.name: Spatiotemporal deduplication into harmonized fire events
method.clustering: Vegetation detections (FIRMS type 0) on the same UTC date whose centres are within 1.0 km (haversine) belong to one event, regardless of sensor (MODIS / VIIRS S-NPP / VIIRS NOAA-20).
method.why_1km_1day: MODIS pixels are ~1 km and VIIRS pixels ~375 m, so the same fire is reported at slightly different centres by each sensor; 1 km absorbs that geolocation/pixel offset without merging neighbouring fires in most of Bangladesh. One UTC day matches the FIRMS daily overpass cycle and the way the archive files are organised; a fire burning across midnight is split, which is a known, stated limitation.
method.frp: Max/median FRP reported per sensor within each event. FRP is never summed across sensors (different pixel sizes) or across events.
method.fire_types: Only FIRMS type 0 (presumed vegetation fire) is harmonized. Types 1 (volcano), 2 (static land) and 3 (offshore) are counted separately as other_types and excluded from event counts.
method.climatology: Monthly mean/std computed over complete years only, and only over years in which every requested sensor was present (the harmonization window). The current partial year is never in the mean. Anomaly z = (events - climatology mean) / sample std; critical when events > mean + 1 SD. Anomalies are reported only for months inside the harmonization window, where the sensor mix matches the baseline; earlier years get no anomaly rather than a misleading one.
method.median_frp: Monthly median FRP is the median over events of each event's maximum FRP (any sensor). Per-sensor medians are of detection FRP.

limitations: Detections are thermal-anomaly pixels, not distinct fires, burned area, or fire severity.
1 km / 1 UTC day clustering is an approximation: a large fire can span several events, and two nearby fires on the same day can be merged into one.
A fire burning across midnight UTC is split into two events (one per day).
VIIRS (375 m) detects smaller/cooler fires that MODIS (1 km) misses, so harmonized counts are still a lower bound on real fire activity, and the sensor mix changes over time.
No cross-sensor FRP calibration is claimed; FRP is never summed across sensors.
Cloud cover, smoke and overpass timing create gaps; a month with no detections is not evidence of no fire.
Monthly means span FIRMS processing versions (e.g. MODIS 6.2, 6.03, 61.03), which may differ slightly in detection.
Counts before a sensor's first full year are not comparable with later years; climatology uses the harmonization window only (years with every sensor present).
